prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its active form that enabled GLP-1-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots rank B017 first, which is unusual, but I do not treat that as merit in itself. The case rests on the discovery. The work moves from proglucagon processing and the isolation of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, through human physiology of incretin secretion and action, to receptor agonists with large effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. It changed a field, and the effect is now visible in clinical practice. It is also mature, with several randomized outcome trials and extensive independent confirmation. Holst (human physiology), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology and the therapeutic rationale) and Mojsov (the active peptide form) are, from the supplied names, the most defensible set that rewards discovery over product development.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Priority for the active GLP-1 form and its insulinotropic role is disputed, and early contributors outside the credited names, such as Habener, may have claims that the supplied list does not capture. A three-person limit also forces us to leave out Knudsen, whose role in designing long-acting acylated analogues is what turned the physiology into drugs. Any citation that leaves out the pharmaceutical step risks reading as incomplete, and one that includes it risks rewarding development more than discovery.

responses.point: Proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating the long-acting agonists as the realised discovery and regarding Mojsov's contribution as contested.
responses.response: I take the point that without liraglutide and semaglutide there would be no clinical transformation, and that the Mojsov question is not settled. I still keep Mojsov over Knudsen. The prize rewards a discovery, and identifying the active peptide and showing how it acts is the discovery step. Knudsen's work is optimization of a known pharmacophore, and I would not want a precedent in which the committee credits industrial analogue design in place of the biological finding. I accept that this is the weakest point of my configuration and that the committee could reasonably end up elsewhere on it.

responses.point: Also proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, and ranks TNF blockade (B018) third as a very mature, arguably overdue translational advance.
responses.response: I agree that B017 should lead, and that the physiology and the drug development are linked. On B018 I disagree about priority for this year. Feldmann and Maini's route from synovial cytokine biology to clinical proof is clear, but it is better described as a translational demonstration. The antibody engineering and the earlier TNF biology sit with people not named, so the attribution is weaker than for GLP-1. Over two decades of use does make it mature, but maturity alone does not argue for ranking it above B006 or B024.

responses.point: Ranks BCR-ABL inhibition (B024) second as the paradigm of molecularly targeted therapy, and ranks the HPV VLP vaccines (B016) above CAR-T cells.
responses.response: I accept that B024 is the better-confirmed field-changing discovery, and I kept it in my top three for that reason. I would not put it above CAR-T on the question of what concept it adds. Imatinib validated a paradigm that other drug programmes had already been pursuing, whereas CAR-T opened a new modality, a living drug. I do agree that the earlier Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL work, not credited here, weakens any prize that is confined to the drug developers. On B016, the priority dispute between Frazer and Zhou, together with the 2008 HPV prize, makes me more cautious than you are.

responses.point: Proposes only June and Sadelain for CAR-T, setting Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer apart as a distinct contribution.
responses.response: That separation seems sound to me, and I raised the same question about Rosenberg in my opening. I would go further. If CAR-T is the prize, the omission of Eshhar from the credited names is a larger attribution gap than the choice between two and three laureates, and I do not see a clean way to fix it within the supplied candidate. That is why I would keep B006 as an alternative rather than prefer it over B017.

uncertainties: Whether Knudsen should replace or accompany Mojsov, and whether the committee wants the citation to cover drug development.
How far priority for the active GLP-1 peptide can be settled from the supplied credit, given possible claims by contributors who are not named.
Whether any CAR-T or BCR-ABL configuration can be made attribution-complete within three names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B017 or the alternatives. My documented ties are to nuclear-receptor and dopamine-neuron work (Ronald Evans, Johan Ericson), and shared KI affiliation and past co-authorship with Svenningsson and El Manira are not connections to any shortlisted candidate.
